title: Lodash
description: Modern utility library for arrays, objects, and functions.

data.text: Lodash provides consistent, cross-browser utilities for common programming tasks using functional programming.

Lodash provides small, well-tested helpers: `debounce` and `throttle` for rate-limiting, `cloneDeep` for a true deep copy, `groupBy` and `keyBy` for reshaping arrays, and `get`/`set` for safe nested access. Used deliberately, they replace hand-rolled utility code.

data.title: Common lodash helpers

data.text: Importing from `lodash` pulls the whole library unless the bundler tree-shakes it. Importing from `lodash-es` (ES modules) or from `lodash/debounce` directly lets the bundler include only what you use, which is often the difference between a few kilobytes and seventy.

data.title: Smaller imports
Interview angle: native JavaScript has absorbed much of lodash
data.text: Many helpers now exist in the platform: `Array.prototype.flat`, `Object.entries`, optional chaining `?.` replaces `get` for simple paths, and `structuredClone` replaces `cloneDeep` for structured data. The honest answer is to reach for lodash when you need its edge cases — `debounce` with `leading`/`trailing` options, `cloneDeep` of exotic values — and use the standard library for the rest.
